landmarks.name: Zuma Rock
landmarks.writeup: A natural monolith located in Niger State, often called the 'Gateway to Abuja' and known for its unique face-like features.

landmarks.name: Olumo Rock
landmarks.writeup: A massive outcrop of granite rocks in Abeokuta, Ogun State, historically used as a fortress by the Egba people.

landmarks.name: National Mosque, Abuja
landmarks.writeup: An important religious site and architectural landmark in Nigeria's capital city.

landmarks.name: Aso Rock
landmarks.writeup: A large rock formation in Abuja, near the Nigerian Presidential Complex and National Assembly.

landmarks.name: Obudu Mountain Resort
landmarks.writeup: A scenic resort in Cross River State known for its cable cars, waterfalls, and temperate climate.

cultural_events.name: Durbar Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional festival celebrated mainly in Northern Nigeria featuring horse parades, music, and cultural displays.

cultural_events.name: Eyo Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A Lagos-based festival involving masquerades dressed in white, honoring the memory of important Lagos figures.

cultural_events.name: New Yam Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual celebration by the Igbo people marking the end of the farming season and the harvest of new yams.

cultural_events.name: Calabar Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: Known as Africa's biggest street party, this December event features music, dance, and cultural exhibitions.

food_writeup: Nigerian cuisine is diverse and flavorful, featuring staples like jollof rice, pounded yam, egusi soup, suya (spiced grilled meat), and akara (bean cakes). Meals often combine rich spices, vegetables, and proteins reflecting the country's ethnic diversity.
brief_history: Nigeria gained independence from British colonial rule in 1960. It has a history marked by diverse ethnic groups, military coups, civil war (1967-1970), and a transition to democratic governance since 1999. It is Africa's most populous country and a major oil producer.

important_people.name: Olusegun Obasanjo
important_people.description: Former Military Head of State and President

important_people.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
important_people.description: Economist and Director-General of the WTO

current_conflicts: Nigeria faces ongoing security challenges including Boko Haram insurgency in the northeast, conflicts between herders and farmers in the Middle Belt, and separatist agitations in the southeast.
